## One gimbal, two mounts

Pan -180…180° · tilt -30…60° · slew 45°/s · FOV 34×20° · range 5–400 m.

ONE gimbal. The same record drives a fixed turret and an airframe mount — the operator's rule: 'design must be the same for both'.

## Airframe and energy (bounding estimates)

**foil-1.111** — span 1.111 m · nose-to-tail 0.7777 m · depth 0.2522 m.

Scaled from `docs/security-2525/xbat-wireframe/xbat.wire.json` (span 38.579462 m · depth 8.627519 m · nose-to-tail 26.2 m), read on the axes that drawing declares: span `x`, depth `y`, nose-to-tail `z`. Operator 2026-09-16: 'make fix wing aircraft 1 m foil and proportional'. 1.111 x 0.7777 is the demo scale of his own FOIL package and is proportional to the full 11.111 x 7.777 to within 0.07 mm on the span. Against the SOURCE drawing it is a 3.07% stretch along the fuselage, which is intentional: his manifest specifies non-uniform scaling and gives the rule for depth, quoted next.

fixed-wing VTOL (quadcopter <-> plane), Quantum-Systems-class · 5 kg · cruise 17 m/s · hover 900 W · cruise 180 W · battery 300 Wh with 20% reserve never spent.

> Brochure-class public figures for a 5 kg VTOL, EXCEPT wingAreaM2, which is no longer asserted: it is derived from the drawing by geometry.planformMethod and gated by frontend/tests/airframe-truth.test.mjs. It read 0.9 m2 until 2026-09-16 — 2.9x the area the aircraft actually has — because the physics record and the drawing were two unconnected descriptions of 'the aircraft' that never met in code. BOUNDING ESTIMATE ONLY - not design evidence.

## The beam, the shield, and the time it takes

Nd:YAG-class continuous emitter, game scale at 1064 nm · 2000 W at the aperture · 0.5 mrad spread · refused past 700 m.

Shield 3 J/cm², airframe 2 J/cm² behind it. A defeated aircraft is **disabled and flown down** at 1.6 m/s — there is no state called destroyed.

**Hold the beam this long.** Computed from the figures above, never typed:

| range | irradiance | shield down | disabled |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 m | 6.29 W/cm² | 0.65 s | 0.97 s |
| 200 m | 2.762 W/cm² | 1.26 s | 1.99 s |
| 300 m | 1.535 W/cm² | 2.13 s | 3.43 s |
| 400 m | 0.971 W/cm² | 3.27 s | 5.33 s |
| 500 m | 0.666 W/cm² | 4.68 s | 7.68 s |
| 600 m | 0.484 W/cm² | 6.38 s | 10.51 s |
| 700 m | 0.366 W/cm² | 8.38 s | 13.84 s |

> BOUNDING ESTIMATE ONLY - not design evidence and not a real weapon. Chosen so the dwell a player feels lands where the game wants it: well under a second in close, a few seconds at the gimbal's declared range, and a slog beyond it. Range matters because the beam spreads and the air absorbs, which is the one physical fact the whole engagement turns on. Fine-track lock is 0.35 s: the director needs that long back on a target before full power, so flicking between targets is a losing tactic and holding is the game.

> Independence Day: the shield absorbs first and nothing reaches the airframe until it fails. Ender's Game and the operator's own words: a defeated aircraft is DISABLED and flown down under control, never deleted in the air. Battle House: it comes back, it is not exterminated.

## Sensor

Profile `pi-baseline` — Edge extraction budget comes out of the frame before the renderer (lib/wire-core/fidelity.ts).

## Targets

Every building door is a pop-up target. Tag it by CAPTURE (store the sensor edge set) then SHOOT (line of sight must reach it). The up-window is not a taste value: a target must stay up longer than the worst swing to reach it (4s at 45°/s for half a turn) plus time to aim and press, or the round is unwinnable by construction. Gated in tests/drone-gimbal.test.mjs. Seed `20260915`, up 14000 ms, down 6000 ms, 3 at once.
